content.value_statement: Feature changes need repeatable validation before release. This skill creates and runs Playwright scenarios, then separates functional results from visual observations.
actual_capabilities: Select a test scope from user input, Git changes, or recent work context.
Create happy-path, edge-case, error-path, and interaction scenarios.
Translate approved scenarios into Playwright MCP browser actions.
Run browser checks and report PASS, FAIL, and WARN results.
Collect optional visual and UX observations without changing functional status.
limitations: It performs browser-based scenario testing, not isolated unit tests.
It requires a runnable local application and Playwright MCP access.
Backend services and test data must be prepared by the project.
Visual observations are advisory unless a visual gate is explicitly enabled.

use_cases.title: Validate a new feature
use_cases.description: Check key user flows after implementing a feature and before requesting review.

use_cases.title: Review changed browser behavior
use_cases.description: Use Git changes to build focused regression scenarios for an affected interface.

use_cases.title: Confirm release readiness
use_cases.description: Run approved end-to-end scenarios and receive a concise functional test report.

prompt_templates.title: Test a page
prompt_templates.prompt: Run scenario tests for the login page and report the results.

prompt_templates.title: Test recent changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the current Git diff to select affected features, create scenarios, and ask for approval before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Test key flows only
prompt_templates.prompt: Test the checkout flow with happy-path scenarios only. Report functional results and any visual observations.

prompt_templates.title: Run focused regression
prompt_templates.prompt: For the profile settings changes, create happy, edge, error, and interaction scenarios. Execute approved tests and retry only failed scenarios once.

output: Scope: files changed in the checkout flow
Visual observations are reported separately from functional results

best_practices: Run the application with test-only data and services before starting browser tests.
Review generated scenarios before execution when the scope is broad.
Use focused scopes to keep regression results easy to diagnose.
anti_patterns: Do not treat this skill as a replacement for isolated unit tests.
Do not run tests against production services or production data.
Do not enable automatic fixes without reviewing the intended scope.

faq.question: Does this skill write unit tests?
faq.answer: No. It runs Playwright-based browser scenarios for feature and regression validation.

faq.question: What does the skill test by default?
faq.answer: It can use an explicit scope, recent Git changes, or recent work context.

faq.question: Does it need approval before running?
faq.answer: Yes, unless the automatic execution option is selected.

faq.question: Can it test backend-dependent features?
faq.answer: Yes, when the required local test services and test data are already available.

faq.question: What are visual findings?
faq.answer: They are separate observations about layout or interface quality and do not normally change functional status.

faq.question: Can it fix failures?
faq.answer: It can attempt a limited fix and rerun when the fix option is explicitly requested.
